- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent forecasts; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model lags in recognizing momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven acceleration.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price peaks in the last 5–7 days; apply a 1–3% upward bias to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
